note: Platforms Romwright lists beyond the gate-report-derived rows of the README support matrix. Tier 1 means a committed gate report measures it; the support matrix generator refuses to print a tier-1 claim whose gate report is missing, so a platform is listed as tier 1 only once someone has looked. Tier 2 is a platform or container that is not fully supported, with the fact that blocks it (`blocker`) and where it was checked (`evidence`); the generator prints these under 'Not supported'. Tier 3 is an input that is supported and has no per-platform gate report of its own: the matrix prints its `claim` as a supported row, and the claim says what was checked and that no gate measures it. Evidence paths are relative to the pinned Ghidra install (docs/upstream-ghidra.md) unless stated otherwise; they were checked against Ghidra 12.1.3. Loaders for 3DS (NCCH/NCSD/CIA), PS3 (SELF/SPRX), Vita (SELF), PSP (PRX), Switch (NCA/XCI) and Xbox 360 (XEX) ship in crates/romwright-core/src/native/ and route through parse_container. Every console processor is modelled: the pinned install ships SPU (GhidraSPU), R5900 with MMI/VU0 (ghidra-emotionengine-reloaded), Allegrex with VFPU and the Xenon VMX128 language; the only blocker left is content whose keys the user has not supplied (the encrypted-container row).

platforms.input: Encrypted console containers (3DS CIA, PS3/Vita SELF, Switch NCA/XCI, Xbox 360 XEX)
platforms.blocker: Retail images are encrypted. The loaders decrypt with bundled public keys where those exist (Xbox 360 XEX retail key, PS3 APP vault, Vita public MetaKeys, 3DS zeros fixed key, and now PSP ~PSP via the long-public KIRK key vault + tag tables in native/kirk_tables.rs), and accept user-supplied keys through a KeyStore (`--keys <file>`): a Switch prod.keys supplies header_key/key_area_key, a PS3 .rap derives the NPDRM title key, a Vita .klic unwraps NPDRM, and a 3DS aes_keys.txt supplies slot0xNN/fixed_system. What remains unreachable is content whose key only the console holds and the user has not dumped — Switch retail NCA/XCI without a prod.keys, 3DS slot-key content without the slot key, PS3/Vita NPDRM without the .rap/.klic. II.1 still forbids any runtime fetch; the keys come only from a file the user provides.
platforms.evidence: crates/romwright-core/src/native/keys.rs (KeyStore) + native/kirk.rs + native/kirk_tables.rs (PSP KIRK vault/tag tables, public constants); import_with(data, keys) on switch/threeds/vita/ps3/psp; tests prove a retail-keyed NCA, an NPDRM SELF via .rap, a klic-wrapped Vita SELF, and a ~PSP round-trip all import.
